title: Home-Style Korean Round Cabbage Kimchi
description: Kimchi is one of Korea's most treasured foods. More than 250 recognised varieties reflect different regions, seasons and family traditions. This home-style recipe brings that tradition to UK kitchens using everyday ingredients.

items.name: Glutinous rice flour (or 2 tbsp plain flour, or 1/2 cup blended cooked rice)
Garlic cloves, finely chopped or grated
Sweet pointed red peppers, finely diced
Spring onions, cut diagonally into 2-3cm lengths
Fish sauce (or vegetarian fish sauce, or 4 tbsp light soy + 1 tbsp white miso)
Gochugaru flakes (coarse Korean chilli flakes, optional)

steps.title: Make the binding paste
steps.body: Boil the squash until tender. Drain and blend until smooth, adding a little cooking water only if needed. Return to the pan. Stir in the chosen starch. Cook for 2-4 minutes until thick. Cool completely.

steps.title: Brine the cabbage
steps.body: Dissolve the salt in the cold water. Add the cabbage. Mix well. Leave for 1 hour, turning once or twice. Rinse well and drain for 15-20 minutes.

steps.title: Mix the raw ingredients
steps.body: Combine the cooled paste with all raw ingredients. If using gochugaru, leave for 20-30 minutes so the flakes hydrate and deepen in colour.

steps.title: Coat the cabbage
steps.body: Add the drained cabbage. Fold and massage gently until every piece is evenly coated.

steps.title: Pack the jars
steps.body: Pack firmly into sterilised jars. Leave about 2.5cm headspace. Press down to remove air pockets and keep the vegetables below the liquid.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.body: Leave at room temperature for 12-24 hours. When small bubbles appear and the aroma turns lightly tangy, refrigerate. Start the fermentation tracker below once jars are packed.

stages.label: Fresh
stages.description: Fresh, crisp, lightly fermented — still settling in

stages.label: Best window
stages.description: Balanced, tangy, still crunchy — the best time to eat it

stages.label: Past peak
stages.description: More sour and softer, with possible slight bitterness

stages.label: Well past best
stages.description: Very sour and soft by now — better used cooked into dishes like kimchi jjigae than eaten fresh

variations.name: Traditional
variations.description: Use napa cabbage or daikon and increase the gochugaru.

variations.name: Spring greens
variations.description: Replace part of the cabbage with pak choi, mustard greens or spinach.

variations.name: Orchard
variations.description: Add julienned pear and toasted sesame seeds for a sweeter, fruitier kimchi.

notes.label: Storage
notes.body: Refrigerate once fermented. Use a clean utensil and keep the vegetables submerged. Best enjoyed within two weeks for crunch and freshness.

notes.label: Serving
notes.body: Serve with steamed rice, tofu, bibimbap, noodles, fried rice, Korean pancakes or grilled vegetables.
